source.title: The AI Scaling Wall of Diminishing Returns: Of LLMs, Electric Dogs, and General Relativity

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. The figures are not rendered in the supplied text, and some equations have garbled formatting.
record.tranche_reason: It fits MMLU-Pro accuracy against training compute, rather than measuring held-out pretraining loss or compute-optimal allocations as the cited scaling-law papers do.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own MMLU-Pro-versus-compute fit and extrapolations, which bear on downstream predictability (V6). It does not directly test held-out loss scaling, small-run prediction of larger-run loss, compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, or architecture sensitivity. Its comparison of curve families concerns the accuracy-compute projection, not the cited loss-scaling laws. The cited studies' results are not treated as this paper's results.
record.test_reason: This is an opinion essay. It takes Hoffmann's compute exponent (α = 0.34) as given and maps it into a sigmoid accuracy curve anchored to two models (Llama 3 70B, Claude 4.1). The ±25% band is imposed, not estimated. The 90%/95% thresholds and β ≈ 0.55 are properties of this constructed curve, not measurements. The only empirical content is an unquantified remark that plotted frontier models 'cluster along the predicted trend.' No model list, scores, compute values or goodness-of-fit are given. So the paper applies the scaling law to make a projection rather than testing any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The author builds a sigmoid MMLU-Pro-versus-compute curve by transforming Hoffmann's α = 0.34 and anchoring it to Llama 3 70B and Claude 4.1. He reads its flattening, with ~1-2 pp per decade at high compute, as showing an intrinsic 'scaling wall': scale alone will not reach AGI, and progress must come from efficiency, architecture and deployment. These are presented as projections from that construction, not as independently fitted empirical evidence.
record.recipe_differences: It converts a cited loss-scaling formulation into a fitted MMLU-Pro accuracy-versus-compute curve, using two model anchors and a sigmoid; it does not measure held-out loss across parameter, token, or compute sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The study explores sigmoid, Gompertz, Richards, and Morgan-Mercer-Flodin curve families; it says the sigmoid is most stable and interpretable and that the families converge closely at high compute.
record.problems: The paper gives no table of underlying model-level MMLU-Pro scores or compute values in the supplied text. The accuracy curve is constructed from two named anchors, and the reported thresholds and tail behavior are fit-based projections. No controls are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported model-level results were extracted: the supplied text gives no individual plotted values or names beyond the two curve anchors.

untested.parts: No loss measurements; Hoffmann's exponent is assumed.
No loss fits on small runs used to predict larger runs.
No other modalities or training regimes.
There is no quantified fit of real model MMLU-Pro scores against compute. Predictability from loss is not measured.
There are no comparisons of fitting choices for loss laws or for optimal splits.

missing.what: The claim that returns fall ~3.6x per decade (~12 pp at 10 YFLOP, ~3 pp at 100, <1 pp beyond 1000). These are also outputs of the constructed curve, not data.
missing.locator: What Does It All Mean - Part I

record.verdict_notes: This is a non-peer-reviewed essay. The reader's 'tests'/T2 classification and its V6 supports/limits_scope and V7 challenges labels are withdrawn. The quantitative values are derived from assumptions (the borrowed exponent, two anchors, an imposed band), so they cannot support or challenge the versions. The visual statement that frontier models lie on the curve is too unquantified to serve as evidence for V6.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether loss laws fitted on small runs predict much larger runs.
The compute-optimal parameter/token split and its growth with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture details on loss at fixed parameter count.
Scaling in other modalities and training regimes.
Other downstream benchmarks and whether performance is predictable from pretraining loss; the analysis is limited to MMLU-Pro accuracy versus compute.
The study compares curve families for its accuracy-compute projection only; it does not test parameter-counting, training schedule, data, loss-fit exponents, or compute-optimal allocation.

rows.subject: Frontier models (aggregate as described)
rows.operation_detail: Fits MMLU-Pro accuracy against total training compute and describes the plotted frontier-model trend.
rows.measure: MMLU-Pro accuracy versus total training compute
rows.value: Frontier models cluster along the predicted trend.
rows.uncertainty: α = 0.34 ± 0.08 for the fitted curve band
rows.locator: Figure 1 caption and “The Math Of Diminishing Returns”
rows.note: The text describes the trend but supplies no individual frontier-model scores in the provided extraction.
rows.check: This is a qualitative visual statement with no model names, scores, compute values or fit statistic. The curve was not fitted to these models; it was built from Hoffmann's α plus two anchors. α = 0.34 ± 0.08 is an assumed input with an imposed ±25% band, not an uncertainty of the result.

rows.subject: Early models (aggregate as described)
rows.operation_detail: Compares plotted MMLU-Pro accuracy with the fitted accuracy-compute curve.
rows.measure: Deviation of MMLU-Pro accuracy from the fitted trend
rows.value: Early models sit above the curve; the text suggests architecture or data-quality innovations as possible reasons.
rows.note: The text does not identify the early models or quantify their deviations.
rows.check: The deviation of early models is unquantified and the models are unidentified. The author's architecture/data explanation is speculation.

rows.subject: MMLU-Pro accuracy-compute fit
rows.operation_detail: Constructs a sigmoid accuracy-compute curve anchored to Llama 3 70B and Claude 4.1.

conditions.value: Llama 3 70B (~1 billion PFLOP); Claude 4.1 (~10 billion PFLOP)

rows.measure: Projected MMLU-Pro accuracy at total training compute
rows.value: The fitted curve reaches 90% at roughly 10¹⁰ PFLOP and approaches an asymptote near 95%; reaching 95% is estimated to require 5.6 × 10¹⁰ PFLOP.
rows.uncertainty: α = 0.34 ± 0.08; the text describes this as a ±25% variation
rows.locator: Figure 1 caption; “The Math Of Diminishing Returns”; “What Does It All Mean - Part I”
rows.note: These are fitted projections, not reported held-out loss measurements. The curve is anchored to two named models.
rows.check: This is not a result. The 90% at ~1e10 PFLOP, the ~95% asymptote and the 5.6e10 PFLOP figure are outputs of a curve constructed from an assumed exponent and two anchor points. The uncertainty is an imposed ±25% on α.

rows.subject: MMLU-Pro accuracy-compute fit
rows.operation_detail: Fits the tail of the derivative of accuracy with respect to log compute.
rows.measure: Marginal MMLU-Pro accuracy gain per decade of compute
rows.value: β = 0.554 ± 0.004 (2σ); the text says each decade of additional compute yields only ≈ 1-2 percentage points of improvement.
rows.locator: Figure 2 caption; “The Math Of Diminishing Returns”
rows.note: The reported quantity is derived from the fitted accuracy-compute curve.
rows.check: β = 0.554 is fitted to the derivative of the author's own constructed curve, not to model data. It is a property of the construction, not an observation of downstream scaling.

rows.subject: MMLU-Pro accuracy-compute curve families
rows.operation_detail: Explores sigmoid, Gompertz, Richards, and Morgan-Mercer-Flodin curve families for the accuracy-compute fit.
rows.measure: Stability and high-compute convergence of fitted accuracy-compute curves
rows.value: The sigmoid is described as the most stable and interpretable fit across anchors; the curve families are said to converge closely at high compute.
rows.locator: Section beginning “To project Hoffmann’s loss-scaling law”; Figure 1 discussion
rows.note: This comparison is for the study's accuracy-compute projection, not for held-out loss exponents or compute-optimal allocations.
rows.check: This compares functional families for the author's projection tool, with no reported fit statistics. It does not concern exponents or compute-optimal splits of loss laws, so it does not bear on V7. 'Absent' is not a meaningful state here.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
